qualification_scope: Official binary identity and CLI capabilities, upstream source compatibility review, and deterministic wrapper environment regression; no live provider authentication or tunnel provisioning.
compatibility_findings: AWS workload identity is opt-in and mutually exclusive with static API keys. Prodex removes both ambient AWS identity-selection variables before its existing static-key probes and child startup.
Static-key authentication and the existing run/config/health/log flags remain available. The runtime minimum and native version/capability policy are unchanged.
Loopback Harpoon templates and local upload tracing remain explicit upstream opt-ins; Prodex does not enable them or change its MCP endpoint configuration.
successful_probes: doctor --json with wrapper-shaped YAML, synthetic key and loopback-only mocked MCP/OAuth endpoints

regression.baseline: Failed before the environment filter change; conflicting AWS identity provider remained in the child environment.
regression.official_binary_confirmation: The official binary rejects ambient AWS identity selectors alongside a synthetic static key, then passes all mandatory doctor checks after those selectors are removed. All probe destinations were loopback mocks; no real control-plane authentication, model turn or tunnel provisioning occurred.
